title: Declare a test URN header in every test file

facts.note: Test files are identified by the *.test.* / *.spec.* naming pattern, in any language (stack-neutral obligation).
Only test files are in scope; source files are excluded. Applies to every in-scope test file, whether new, edited or unchanged.
Produced by bun_tester_discipline_detector parsing the leading comment block of each scanned test file.

fires: A new *.test.* file is created without a `// URN: test:...` line in its leading comment block.
An existing, unchanged *.spec.* file scanned by the coverage gate has its URN comment placed after the import statements.
A test file's leading comment block has a `URN:` field whose value does not use the `test:` scheme.
A wagon-level test file covering several acceptances is relied on for coverage but has no URN header.
doesNotFire: A non-test source file (not *.test.* / *.spec.*) — that is the coder extension's business.
A test file inside a vendored or build directory.
A test file whose filename does not encode an acceptance id but whose header carries a valid `test:` URN.

given: Any `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*` file (new or existing) outside vendored/build dirs
when: it is in the test-file scan scope
then: Its leading comment block, above the first real code line (imports included), carries `// URN: test:{wagon}:{feature}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}`.
prefer: Bind via the header, keeping the file layout; multi-acceptance files need no rename.
avoid: A URN below imports or code — it reads as missing.
Encoding acceptance ids in filenames instead of the header; filenames are never parsed.
unless: Not a test file (source files are the coder extension's business).
In a vendored or build directory (never scanned).
why: The URN is the coverage gate's foundation: without it the gate cannot attribute the test or report coverage, and marks the acceptance uncovered while the test passes. Header, not filename, because wagon-level files cover several acceptances; a filename rule would force renaming the suite.
evidence: bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no missing/invalid URN finding for the test file.
Reviewer sees `// URN: test:{wagon}:{feature}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}` in the leading comment block before the first import/code line.
verifier_detail: Detector parses the file's leading comment block (Bun line comments `//`) for a `URN:` field and requires the `test:` scheme; format `test:{wagon}:{feature}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}`.
The header region ends at the first line of real code, so a URN below the imports is treated as missing.
Identity is never derived from the filename; header is authoritative (header_authority).
Scan scope: all *.test.* / *.spec.* files (not only changed ones); vendored and build directories are never scanned.
Stack-neutral obligation with a Bun-specific line-comment detector; realized by `bun_tester_discipline_detector` (implementation type: validator).
Without a test URN there is no edge from the test to anything in the graph; the gate cannot attribute the test and reports its acceptance as uncovered.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

Bun realization of the core obligation `tester.filename.test-carries-urn-identity`; core carries no shared alias, so lineage is stated here. Core's counterpart is explicit that identity is the HEADER, not the filename, and this realization follows that exactly.

Header-over-filename is a deliberate, load-bearing choice and the same conclusion issue #1783 reached independently for backend TypeScript: a one-acceptance-per-filename rule would force a rename of the entire suite to satisfy a tool.
Terms: test_urn = `test:{wagon}:{feature}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}` in the leading comment block; header_authority = identity is the header, not filename, so wagon-level files need no rename.

sharedNodes.text: Disposition strict: the extension (atdd-bun) fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
